title: Invertibility of the specified section-pullback regular-unit mate
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], let $X,Y$ be schemes in universe $u$, and let $f:X\to Y$ be any scheme morphism. Use the fixed small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], with objects and module sections in universe $u+1$ and morphisms in universe $u$. Write $R_T$ for the section-ring sheaf of the pulled-back coefficients on $T$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients, def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence]. Use exactly the coefficient map $c:R_Y\to f_*R_X$, section-module functors $L=f^*_{\rm sec}$ and $P=f_{*,\rm sec}$ and specified adjunction $L\dashv P$ of [def-pd-section-module-operations-data]. Module tensors are the sheafified balanced tensors [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], and their units are the regular modules $R_T$. Let $P$ carry its uniquely normalized lax structure: its tensor maps send every local pure tensor over $V$ to the same pure tensor over $V\times_YX$, and its regular-unit map is $c$. Let $L$ have the oplax structure obtained as mate under the specified adjunction [lem-sfb-adjunction-oplax-mate], and write $a_M:M\to PLM$ for the adjunction unit. The oplax unit $\eta_L:L(R_Y)\to R_X$, defined as the adjunct of $c:R_Y\to P(R_X)$ under this adjunction, is an isomorphism. In particular this concerns the unit of the chosen oplax structure, rather than asserting merely that the two regular modules are abstractly isomorphic.

proof.text: The geometric siteMap is continuous by the operations transport construction. Base change preserves finite limits and hence terminal objects, so the over-site functor is final. These instances discharge exactly the site hypotheses of the final-ringed-unit theorem, giving invertibility of the unit of the specified mate adjunction, including zero rings and empty schemes.
